questions.question: What happens if your vehicle's ABS stops working?

options.text: You will have no brakes at all.
Your brakes will still work.
You should only use the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your brakes will still work.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard. If your ABS breaks, your regular brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, outside convex mirrors should let the driver see:

options.text: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
Where the front of each front tire touches the ground.
The top of the bus.
The muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, outside convex mirrors should show at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: While students exit a school bus, the driver should watch to make sure they:

options.text: Leave in pairs.
Don't get caught on the handrail or door.
Don't talk while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't get caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Students can be hurt or killed if their clothing, accessories, or bodies get caught on a handrail or door while leaving the bus. The driver should watch closely to make sure all students exit safely.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located on a bus?

options.text: On the right side of the bus.
On the steering wheel.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use this mirror to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: How is student safety best maintained in general?

options.text: Keep students on the bus.
Let some students leave the bus.
Let students leave the bus and scatter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest and easiest to control when they stay on the bus. Keep students on the bus as long as it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When picking up students, park at least 10 feet away because:

options.text: You can see their movements clearly.
It will be hard to park any closer.
Students need the exercise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see their movements clearly.
questions.explanation: Park with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students. This lets you watch the students as they walk to the bus.

questions.question: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, what should happen?

options.text: Students should stay on the bus.
Students should be evacuated to a spot near the bus.
Students should be evacuated and moved far from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should be evacuated and moved far from the bus.
questions.explanation: If a bus stalls on railroad tracks, evacuate everyone immediately. Move students far from the bus at an angle away from oncoming trains to avoid flying debris.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus for a hazard, the driver should:

options.text: Ask students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
Take time to decide if evacuation is needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
questions.explanation: If time allows, contact your dispatcher before evacuating. Make the evacuation decision quickly.

questions.question: After students leave the bus at school, the driver should:

options.text: Assume students took all their belongings.
Assume students cleared the doorway right away.
Walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students.
Turn off the dispatch radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students exit, walk through the bus to look for any students who may be sleeping or hiding. Also check for items left behind.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Stay in control on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in control on slippery surfaces.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking when you brake hard on slippery roads. This helps you keep control of your vehicle. Drive and brake a vehicle with ABS the same way as one without ABS.

questions.question: Before leaving a bus stop, a driver should:

options.text: Check that no students are running to catch the bus.
Check that students have put their backpacks in the aisle.
Check that students have opened the emergency vent.
Check that students are facing the back of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that no students are running to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Before driving away from a bus stop, the driver must check that no students are running to board the bus.

questions.question: School buses:

options.text: Never have ABS brakes.
Only have ABS brakes if children under 10 will be on the bus.
May have ABS brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have ABS brakes.
questions.explanation: Most school buses made after 1998 or 1999 have anti-lock braking systems (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: The overhead inside rearview mirror should show:

options.text: The rear tires.
All students on the bus.
The floor of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror should be set so the driver can see all students on the bus, including those sitting right behind the driver.

questions.question: When dropping off students at school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if leaving the driver's seat.
Read while students leave the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When students get off at school, the driver must turn off the engine to secure the bus. If the driver leaves the driver's seat, they must remove the key. The driver must watch while students exit.

questions.question: Bus stops may be changed by:

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: The local school district sets official bus routes and stops. Drivers cannot change a stop location without written approval from a district official.

questions.question: If a student drops an item near a stopped bus, they should:

options.text: Quickly pick up the item.
Leave the item behind.
Ask the driver to pick it up.
Have another student get it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could move out of the driver's sight. Instead, students should leave the danger zone, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and there is no nearby shelter, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby ditch.
To the closest tree.
Near a river.

questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby ditch.
questions.explanation: If students must leave a bus in the path of a tornado, they should go to a nearby ditch or culvert if no building shelter is available. They should avoid areas with flood risk and stay far enough from the bus so it cannot fall on them.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, the students:

options.text: Must be evacuated.
Should stay on the bus but move away from the fire.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be evacuated.
questions.explanation: If there is a fire on the bus or any threat of fire, the driver must evacuate all students immediately.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a driver should check that all traffic has stopped before:

options.text: Opening the door and signaling students to come forward.
Turning on the alternating red lights.
Pulling to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and signaling students to come forward.
questions.explanation: Before opening the door to let students board, the driver must make sure all surrounding traffic has stopped.

questions.question: When approaching a bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Honk the horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly.
questions.explanation: A bus driver should always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.
